filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Set camera parameters for the current mesh. The camera is stored and used by other filters such as 'Vertex Quality from Camera'.

parameters.help: Type of camera projection.

filters.name: Set Raster Camera
filters.shortDescription: Set the camera parameters for the current raster.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Set camera parameters for the current raster, from a viewpoint, a direction and a focal length, or from a view: the camera of a 3D view, by default the current one, with its projection, field of view and roll. Either way the camera is made for the raster's own image size, centred on it.

The camera from a view is a starting point for aligning a photo to a mesh: navigate a 3D view until the model looks as it does in the photo, and give that camera to the raster.

parameters.label: From a view
parameters.help: Take the camera of a view instead of the viewpoint, direction and focal length below.

parameters.label: View camera
parameters.help: The view whose camera the raster gets (MeshLab.CameraState JSON).

parameters.label: Viewpoint
parameters.help: Camera position in world space.

parameters.label: View direction
parameters.help: Camera viewing direction.

parameters.label: Focal length (mm)
parameters.help: Camera focal length in millimeters.

parameters.label: Sensor width (mm)
parameters.help: Camera sensor width in millimeters. For an orthographic camera, the width of the view volume in world units, and the focal length plays no part.

parameters.label: Projection
parameters.help: Perspective or orthographic camera. 'Keep current' uses the projection of the raster's present camera, and perspective when it has none.

parameters.label: Map to color

filters.name: Orient Vertex Normals by Cameras
filters.shortDescription: Reorient vertex normals to point toward the cameras that see them best.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Reorient vertex normals using visible rasters. For each vertex, the best camera is chosen among all visible rasters and the normal is oriented to face toward that camera. If the per-vertex attribute 'correspondences' exists (from Bundler .out imports), the original Bundler camera indices are used instead.

filters.name: Set Camera to View Selection
filters.shortDescription: Position the camera in front of the current selection, facing it, so that the selection fills the view.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Compute a camera that frames the current selection. The camera stands in front of the selection, on the side its normals point to, and looks back at it along the average of the face (or vertex) normals; it is as far as a sphere around the selected vertices needs to fill the field of view. The 3D view moves to the camera, the camera state JSON is written to the log and returned as `cameraState`, and the current raster, if there is one, gets the camera for its own image size.

parameters.label: Margin factor
parameters.help: Viewport margin multiplier. 1.0 = tight fit, 1.5 = some padding.

parameters.label: FOV (degrees)
parameters.help: Vertical field of view in degrees.

parameters.label: Projection
parameters.help: Perspective or orthographic camera. 'Keep current' uses the projection of the current raster's camera, and perspective when there is none. The framing is the same either way: the camera sees the same height at the target.

parameters.label: Use face normals
parameters.help: Average face normals to determine the view direction. If no faces are selected, falls back to vertex normals.

filters.name: Set Camera from Direction
filters.shortDescription: Position the camera looking toward a target from an explicit direction.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Compute a camera that looks toward a target (mesh bounding box center or current raster) from an explicit world-space direction. The camera is as far as a sphere around the target needs to fill the field of view. The 3D view moves to the camera, the camera state JSON is written to the log and returned as `cameraState`, and the current raster, if there is one, gets the camera for its own image size.

parameters.label: View direction
parameters.help: World-space direction from camera to target.

parameters.label: Target
parameters.help: What the camera should look at.

parameters.label: Margin factor
parameters.help: Viewport margin multiplier. 1.0 = tight fit, 2.0 = zoom out.

parameters.label: FOV (degrees)
parameters.help: Vertical field of view in degrees.

parameters.label: Projection
parameters.help: Perspective or orthographic camera. 'Keep current' uses the projection of the current raster's camera, and perspective when there is none. The framing is the same either way: the camera sees the same height at the target.

filters.name: Set Camera to Frame from Viewpoint
filters.shortDescription: Turn and zoom a camera, without moving it, so that the scene, a layer or the selection fills its image exactly.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Keeps the viewpoint of a camera -- by default the current 3D view's -- and changes only where it looks and its field of view, so that the target fills the image exactly: centred, and touching its top and bottom or its sides, whichever is the tighter. This is View > Frame Scene from Here as a filter. The camera keeps its up direction, so it does not roll.

**Image shape** *Camera's own* frames for the image the camera was for, the width over height that the camera state records (`viewport_px`, which the 3D view writes). *Fit to the target* lets the target choose it too, so that it touches all four sides: the image a snapshot of exactly the target's shape would have, which is returned as `aspect`.

The 3D view moves to the camera, which is also returned as `cameraState`, a MeshLab.CameraState document, with the field of view as `fovYDeg`. Nothing is changed when the target cannot be framed from the viewpoint: a perspective camera is needed, no part of the target may be behind the viewpoint or nearer than the near plane would be, and the field of view has to stay between 10 and 120 degrees.

parameters.label: Camera
parameters.help: The camera whose viewpoint is kept (MeshLab.CameraState JSON).

parameters.label: Target
parameters.help: What fills the image: the vertices of the visible layers, of the current layer, or of its selection.

parameters.label: Image shape
parameters.help: Frame for the camera's own image, or let the target choose the image's width over height too.

filters.name: Align Current Raster to Mesh by Point Correspondences
filters.shortDescription: Correct the current raster's camera from points on the mesh and the pixels where the photo shows them.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Refines where the current raster's camera stands and looks, and optionally its focal length, so that it projects each point onto its pixel: the camera that minimizes the root mean square distance between them, in pixels. The raster's camera has to be roughly right to start with; *Set Raster Camera* from a view gives one.

The principal point, the pixel size and the lens are left as they are: they are the calibration's. Three pairs are needed, four with the focal length; more are averaged.

**Correspondences** is a JSON array of pairs, each a world-space point and a pixel of the image the raster's camera is made for (its viewport, the size of the photo as MeshLab shows it, undistorted when the raster has a lens): `[{"point": [x, y, z], "pixel": [u, v]}, ...]`, with the pixel's origin at the top-left corner of the image, y down, and pixel centres at k + 0.5.

The error before and after, root mean square and maximum, and each pair's, are logged and returned as `rmsBefore`, `rmsAfter`, `maxAfter` and `pairErrors`.

parameters.label: Correspondences
parameters.help: Pairs of a world-space point and the image pixel that shows it, as a JSON array of {"point": [x, y, z], "pixel": [u, v]}; pixels from the top-left corner, y down.

parameters.label: Estimate focal length
parameters.help: Fit the focal length too; it needs four pairs.

filters.name: Align Current Raster to Mesh by Mutual Information
filters.shortDescription: Refine the current raster's camera so that a rendering of the visible layers matches its photo.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Refines where the current raster's camera stands and looks, and optionally its focal length, by maximizing the mutual information between the photo, in grey levels, and a rendering of the visible layers through the camera: the method of Corsini et al. 2009. It is a refinement: the camera has to be close already, within a few pixels, as *Align Current Raster to Mesh by Point Correspondences* leaves it. The principal point, the pixel size and the lens are left as they are.

The rendering is made on the CPU, at a working resolution whose longest side is **Resolution**, and shows one of: the surface normal's component up the image (*Normal Map*, which needs nothing but normals); the vertex color blended into that by the square of its red, meant to hold ambient occlusion (*Combined*, which is the normal map where the vertex color is white); or the vertex color's red (*Vertex Color*). Rendered background counts 1 / **Background weight** as much as the rest, and pixels the photo does not cover, as an undistorted photo's corners, not at all.

The camera's parameters are scaled so that a unit step moves the mesh's projection by about a pixel of the working resolution: **Expected error** is how far the optimizer first looks, and it stops when its steps fall below **Tolerance**, or after **Max evaluations** renderings. The mutual information before and after, in bits, the number of renderings, and how far the camera moved the mesh's projection in the raster's pixels are logged and returned as `informationBefore`, `informationAfter`, `evaluations` and `displacement`.

parameters.label: Rendering
parameters.help: What the rendering of the layers shows, to compare with the photo.

parameters.label: Estimate focal length
parameters.help: Let the focal length change too.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.help: The longest side, in pixels, of the photo and the rendering as they are compared; a larger photo is scaled down.

parameters.label: Max evaluations
parameters.help: The most renderings the optimizer may make.

parameters.label: Expected error (px)
parameters.help: How far, in pixels of the working resolution, the optimizer first looks.

parameters.label: Tolerance (px)
parameters.help: The optimizer stops when its steps move the projection by less than this, in pixels of the working resolution.

parameters.label: Background weight
parameters.help: Rendered background counts 1 / this as much as the rest; 0 leaves it out.
